maya: FYI I'm finishing the initial bring-up for Cerberus-70B v0.9 on dedicated infra. Quick findings below, need infra/quant eyes.

maya: Summary — long-window behavior looks fine under light load, but after a model reload (hot-swap) we see KV cache prefix misses on sequences > 48k tokens. Repro steps and numbers below. :eyes:

sam: can you paste the minimal repro and logs?

maya: repro (run on canary GPU pool):
```bash
# spike a long-prefill, then reload model and continue generation
redwoodctl api call --model cerberus-70b:v0.9 --seq 65536 --prompt-file long_prompt.txt --trace kvcache > /tmp/cerbus_trace.log
# then trigger model rollout
redwoodctl deploy rollout --model cerberus-70b:v0.9 --strategy canary --canary 5%
```
logs excerpt: 
```
[2025-09-14T18:34:12Z] prefill: tokens=65536 prefix_hash=0x7f3a1d
[2025-09-14T18:35:20Z] model-reload: cerberus-70b:v0.9 staged -> active
[2025-09-14T18:35:21Z] kvcache: fingerprint-mismatch for shard0 (old=0x7f3a1d new=0x8b2f0a) -> treating as miss
[2025-09-14T18:35:21Z] generation: token_mismatch at global_pos=65412 predicted="the" observed="a"
```

maya: Metrics: compared baseline (no reload) vs reload run:
- baseline mismatch rate across eval set (mean 64k) = 0.12%
- after reload mismatch rate = 2.3% (spike concentrated around reload boundary ±2k tokens)
- latency bump ~8-12ms per token for 2k tokens after reload

hiro: hmm looks like fingerprint generation changed under new kernel selection after the hot-swap. Any quant changes in this build?

maya: we tried int4 and int3 configs. Int4 had same behavior, int3 slightly worse but not by much. The interesting bit is regressions only when both: (a) RoPE scale factor modified (we applied small rescale to support 64k) and (b) node reused backend memory (hot-swap) — cold-starts are fine.

eva: can you show fingerprint calc code or trace? maybe hashing used a floating point op that got optimized differently for new kernels.

maya: trace snippet (from /tmp/cerbus_trace.log):
```
kvcache: compute_fingerprint(seq=65536, rot_scale=1.0012) -> 0x7f3a1d
kvcache: compute_fingerprint(seq=65536, rot_scale=1.0000) -> 0x8b2f0a
# fingerprint uses mix(rot_scale, layer_idx, shard_seed) then f32->u64 hashing
```

sam: that f32->u64 path is suspicious. If new kernel switches some vectorized path to use f16 densification, bit pattern changes will follow. We should avoid FP-dependent fingerprinting.

maya: agreed. Proposed immediate mitigations:
- add fingerprint-version header so reloads that change kernel/quant path invalidate caches explicitly
- on canary rollback, force kvcache flush across shards during rollout window
- long-term: switch fingerprint to deterministic integer-only fns (layer idx + prime * rot_scale_fixedpoint)

hiro: I'll open infra ticket to add auto-flush to rollout controller and a rollout flag to force full kvcache invalidation. putting a canary step in the pipeline now.

ci-bot: Deploy canary started for cerberus-70b:v0.9 -> 5% (ids: dpl-20250914-99). Running kvcache-flush=false by default.

eva: for evals, let's run two sweep types:
- micro: 10k prefills across seeds, measure fingerprint diff rate per shard
- macro: full eval with human goldset across 10 long-context prompts (64k, 96k) for quality regressions
I can run micro in the morning.

maya: thanks. I also captured KV snapshots pre/post reload for one run: /artifacts/cerberus/kv-snap-1739512468.tar.gz — contains per-shard checksums and prefix maps.

sam: suggested short-term patch: change rollout controller to set kvcache-invalidate=true if model binary hash changes or if rot_scale param changed by > 1e-4. Also add a test in our integration harness that does rapid reloads with long-prefill and asserts stable fingerprints.

maya: filing follow-up issue: INF-1234 with repro steps, logs, artifacts and suggested patch. Assigning to infra + runtime + ml.

hiro: INF-1234 created, link: https://redwood.internal/infra/issues/INF-1234. I'll add a hotfix PR to the rollout controller.

maya: action items:
1) eva runs micro sweeps tomorrow AM and posts results.
2) hiro lands kvcache-invalidate rollout flag + canary change.
3) sam adds integration test to prevent regressions.
4) maya continues quant comparisons and posts updated mismatch table (int8/int4/int3) by EOD.

sam: ack. I'll also add a small stress test that cycles 3 reloads within 5 minutes to catch flakiness.

maya: thanks all. adding notes to model-onboard doc and will block full rollout until INF-1234 mitigations are in place. :lock: 

eva: :thumbsup: 

ci-bot: Canary patch applied to 5% pool (dpl-20250914-99). Monitoring kvcache-hitratio and mismatch-rate metrics.

maya: will update thread when micro sweep finishes.
